entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is not in dispute that apart from these three cases, Avinash, the husband of Chaitra Patil and her father-in-law have filed a suit in O.S. No.578/2020 before the Prl. Civil Judge and JMFC,
Beldari seeking for a decree of injunction and Avinash has also filed a petition in M.C. No.181/2020 seeking for divorce.
3. It is also not in dispute that Chaitra Patil has also filed a petition in M.C. No.183/2021 seeking for restitution of conjugal rights.

It is also stated that Chaitra Patil has also filed a complaint for offences under Sections 323, 417,
420, 498A, 504 & 506 of the IPC, which has been registered in Crime No.139/2020 and the same is the subject matter of a challenge in Crl.P. No.704/2021 pending before the Principal Bench at Bangalore and in these proceedings the criminal proceedings have been stayed.
5.

In the light of the above indisputable facts, it is rather clear that the parties have resorted to criminal Courts only to intimidate and pressurize the respondents in the corresponding civil proceedings which have been initiated for divorce and for restitution of conjugal rights.

6. I am therefore of the view that no useful purpose will be served by permitting the continuation of these criminal proceedings when admittedly proceedings are pending before the Civil Court in O.S.
No.578/2020 in which a decree for injunction is sought for against the petitioners herein and also in view of the matrimonial NC: 2024:KHC-D:3331 C/W CRL.P No. 100734 of 2022, disputes which have been initiated in M.C. No.181/2020 by the husband for divorce and M.C. No.183/2021 by the wife seeking for restitution of conjugal rights.
7.
Having regard to the fact that the proceedings are being basically used to abuse the process of the law, it would not be appropriate to permit their continuance.
Accordingly, the impugned proceedings are quashed and the petitioners are allowed.
